content.title: About
content.content: The whole wheat hamburger bun (item 2513) is made from whole grain wheat flour, contains bran and seeds, making it more nutritious than standard white buns. It has a soft yet sturdy crumb, a subtle nutty aroma, and a golden crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain buns retain more fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals than their white counterparts.
The bran content aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.
Added seeds such as sunflower or pumpkin increase healthy fat content and give a richer flavor.
Historically, whole grain rolls have been favored in European cuisines as a “healthier” bread option.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports regular bowel movements, helps regulate blood sugar, and contributes to prolonged satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole wheat provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: The bun supplies magnesium, iron, and zinc, important for muscle function, blood formation, and immunity.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact
items.content: Compared with white buns, whole wheat releases glucose more slowly, aiding blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Healthy fats from seeds
items.content: Seeds add polyunsaturated fatty acids that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Grain allergy
items.content: People with wheat or gluten allergy may experience reactions and should avoid this product.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions contain added salt; individuals monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While more nutritious, the bun still provides calories; moderation is key for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Perfect for building hamburgers, sandwiches, and open‑face toast. Toast lightly for a crisp crust, then add lettuce, tomato, cheese, and sauces. Also works well as a side for soups or as a base for appetizers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a cool, dry place in an airtight bag or container. For longer shelf life, store in the refrigerator to prevent drying out and mold growth. Discard if mold or off‑odors appear.
